result.question:
Several work orders on Transformer 1 at site MAIN are sitting in pending approval, and I want them cleared out properly rather than rubber-stamped. Pull every pending-approval work order on Transformer 1 and give me each one's number, description, priority, reported date and any failure code. Then check the latest oil sample and run a dissolved gas fault classification on it. Use the five fault gases (hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene), and use co to check whether the paper is involved.

Sort each pending work order into one of three outcomes:
- Approve it if its description matches the fault the gases currently indicate, or if it is a routine oil sampling job.
- Cancel it if another open or pending work order on Transformer 1 already covers the same job. Keep the older one, cancel the newer one, and put the older work order's number in the cancellation reason.
- Otherwise, leave it pending and tell me in one sentence why.

For any work order you approve that deals with arcing, discharge or tap changer work, raise its priority to 1 if the latest acetylene is above 1 ppm. Don't change the priority of anything else. Finish with a table showing every work order, its outcome and the evidence behind it.

If the latest sample is missing any of the five fault gases, so the classification can't be made reliably, don't approve anything other than routine oil sampling jobs, and don't cancel anything except exact duplicates. Say which gas was missing. If there are no pending-approval work orders at all, say so, and tell me whether the current gas picture justifies raising a new one.
result.answer:
## Pending-approval work orders on Transformer 1 (MAIN)

Only **one** work order exists on Transformer 1, and it was in WAPPR:

| WO | Description | Priority | Reported | Failure code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) — long description also carries addenda for a confirmatory DGA sample, planned outage, monthly resample, and a draft oil-treatment WO that couldn't be created (403) | 1 | 2026-09-30 19:04 UTC | none |

## Latest oil sample (2024-01-19) — DGA classification

All five fault gases present: H2 2850, CH4 7400, C2H6 5470, C2H4 16650, C2H2 7 ppm (CO 32, CO2 1340).

The `interpret_dga` tool returned "LLM unavailable" on two attempts, so I classified manually with the same IEC 60599 / Rogers ratio method:

- C2H2/C2H4 = 0.0004 → code 0 (no arcing/discharge)
- CH4/H2 = 2.60 → code 2
- C2H4/C2H6 = 3.04 → code 2
- **Result: high-temperature thermal fault in oil (T2/T3, ≥700 °C, Rogers case 5)** — ethylene-dominated, acetylene negligible. TDCG 32,409 ppm = IEEE C57.104 Condition 4.
- **Paper involvement: no.** CO is only 32 ppm (CO2/CO ≈ 42), so cellulose is not in the fault path; this is a metallic hot spot in oil — consistent with coking/overheated OLTC contacts.

## Outcomes

| WO | Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | **Approved** (now APPR) | Description (OLTC contact wear/coking) matches the T2/T3 thermal-in-oil fault indicated by the gases; no other WO on Transformer 1 exists, so no duplicate to cancel. Tap-changer work with acetylene 7 ppm > 1 ppm qualifies for priority 1 — it was **already priority 1**, so no change was made. |

Nothing was cancelled (no duplicates) and nothing was left pending.

Two things worth noting: the DGA tool outage means the classification above is my manual ratio calculation rather than the server's, though the arithmetic is unambiguous; and the WO's addenda record that the separate oil-treatment/degassing and monthly-resample WOs still need manual creation, since the WO store rejected them earlier.
